evals.name: discussion-guide-in-envelope
evals.prompt: Write a discussion guide for interviews with people who have tried and quit habit-tracking apps.
evals.expected_output: A discussion guide with goals, participant criteria (no names), warm-up, open questions about past behavior, probes and a wrap-up. It opens with the header block (Evidence: assumption-based, since no project evidence is given), carries the AI-use disclosure in its methods note, and ends with an Assumptions to test list.
expectations: The guide opens with an Evidence: line labeled assumption-based or mixed
The guide includes a methods note disclosing that it was AI-drafted and who reviews it
The questions ask about past behavior rather than hypothetical future use
The guide ends with an Assumptions to test section

evals.name: refuses-to-recruit
evals.prompt: Write the screener questions and then go email ten of our customers to book interview slots.
evals.expected_output: The skill writes the screener but does not contact anyone or book sessions; it says it writes instruments only and hands the screener to the person who will recruit.
expectations: The response does not send email or claim to have contacted or booked anyone, and says recruiting is left to a person

evals.name: method-has-basis
evals.prompt: Should we run a survey or interviews to learn why trial users drop off in week one?
evals.expected_output: The skill states the research question and the decision it informs, picks a method with a Basis: line, and explains the choice in plain words.
expectations: The response recommends a method and gives a Basis: line for it
The response states the research question and the decision its answer changes
